report.headline: CLEAR Outcomes met its primary MACE-4 endpoint with a narrow success, showing a modest 10% relative risk reduction consistent with LDL-C lowering but with safety signals including tendon rupture.
report.summary: The CLEAR Outcomes trial randomized approximately 14,000 statin-intolerant patients with LDL-C ≥100 mg/dL to bempedoic acid 180 mg daily or placebo and followed them for a median of 42 months. The trial was designed to detect a 15% relative risk reduction (RRR) in the MACE-4 composite (cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, coronary revascularization) with 1,620 planned events. Based on the CLEAR Wisdom phase 3 biomarker study showing a placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction of -17.4% from a baseline of 120.4 mg/dL, the calculator predicted an expected hazard ratio of 0.896 (10.4% RRR) with only 60% power, below the conventional 80% threshold. The minimum detectable effect at 80% power was HR 0.87 (13% RRR), exceeding the expected effect. The press release announced a statistically significant reduction in MACE-4, consistent with the narrow_success prediction. Safety signals include tendon rupture (0.5% vs 0% placebo) and gout, while myalgia was lower with bempedoic acid (4.7% vs 7.2%). Mendelian randomization supports ACLY inhibition causality (HR 0.82 per genetic score), though Open Targets shows no direct genetic association for coronary artery disorder. Confidence is medium given the modest effect size and limited power.

report.what_would_change_this: The full published results with the observed hazard ratio, confidence interval, and p-value would confirm whether the effect size matches the predicted 10% RRR or is larger/smaller; detailed safety data on tendon rupture and gout incidence at scale would clarify the risk-benefit balance.
report.readthrough_note: The modest LDL-C lowering (-17.4%) in statin-intolerant patients translates to a small expected CV benefit; other ACLY inhibitors or combination therapies (e.g., with ezetimibe) showing greater LDL-C reduction may achieve more robust outcomes. The tendon rupture signal warrants monitoring in other bempedoic acid programmes.

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: Open Targets shows ACLY genetic association score 0.0 with 0 evidence items for coronary artery disorder (f_af5e85be6cc1f6). However, a Mendelian randomization study published before the evidence cut-off (pmid:30865797, 2019-03-01) demonstrates that an ACLY genetic score is associated with lower plasma LDL-C and lower risk of cardiovascular events (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.78-0.87, n=654,783) (f_e5f10161df91fe). This genetic evidence supports a causal role of ACLY inhibition in coronary disease.

mechanism.notes: LDL-C change from CLEAR Wisdom (statin-intolerant population matching CLEAR Outcomes) used as primary biomarker input. apoB, non-HDL-C, and hsCRP changes from CLEAR Serenity (phase 3, 180 mg, placebo-adjusted at week 12) as no outcome-trial biomarker data available at evidence cut-off (2022-12-07). Follow-up of 3.5 years (42 months) from design paper (pmid:33470195) described as 'projected median treatment exposure'; actual median follow-up unknown. Planned events 1620 from same design paper. No SBP change data available. Trial not yet read out at cut-off.

for.text: Calculator predicts HR 0.896 (10.4% RRR) based on placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction of -17.4% in statin-intolerant population (CLEAR Wisdom) with baseline 3.114 mmol/L, yielding LDL-C equivalent reduction 0.542 mmol/L; CTT meta-analysis supports ~22% RRR per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction.

Trial design appropriate: 1620 events planned (f_d3ae35ede6f45d), 3.5-year median follow-up (f_abc0900e9c995a), placebo-controlled, standard MACE-4 endpoint (f_74eaab4866bbe4, f_c1f4a63bc89e7f), large sample ~14,000 (f_66a8b978b68f8d).

against.text: Power only 60.1% for expected effect; minimum detectable effect HR 0.87 (13% RRR) exceeds expected HR 0.896. Substantial chance (40%) trial fails to reach significance even if true effect matches prediction.

hypotheses.would_settle: Actual trial results (HR, CI, p-value) when published.

for.text: Expected RRR only 10.4% (HR 0.896) vs design assumption of 15% RRR (f_fb635c62379ee9). Power 60.1% < 80% conventional threshold. MDE HR 0.87 > expected HR 0.896.
LDL-C reduction in statin-intolerant population (CLEAR Wisdom) is -17.4% (f_77a23c173de6bc) vs -21.4% in broader phase 3 (CLEAR Serenity, f_0b324ba5d602e1), yielding smaller expected benefit.

against.text: Mendelian randomization supports ACLY inhibition → lower LDL-C → lower CV events (HR 0.82 per genetic score, f_e5f10161df91fe), suggesting mechanism is valid and effect size plausible.

hypotheses.would_settle: Observed HR and CI from trial readout; if HR ~0.90 with CI excluding 1, effect is real but modest.

for.text: Open Targets genetic association score for ACLY is 0.0 with 0 evidence items for coronary artery disorder (f_af5e85be6cc1f6).

against.text: Mendelian randomization study (pmid:30865797, 2019-03-01, before cut-off) shows ACLY genetic score associated with lower LDL-C and lower CV events (HR 0.82, CI 0.78-0.87) (f_e5f10161df91fe). This provides direct human genetic evidence for causality.

hypotheses.would_settle: Consistency of observed trial HR with genetic prediction (HR 0.82).

against.text: LDL-C is established causal biomarker for ASCVD (CTT meta-analyses, MR studies). Calculator uses LDL-C as basis with expected HR 0.896.

hypotheses.would_settle: N/A — LDL-C causality not in doubt.

for.text: Tendon rupture reported in 0.5% on bempedoic acid vs 0% placebo in CLEAR Outcomes (f_f1b079c609ee14). Gout signal in CLEAR Harmony (f_36d2ad1fd3b9e1). Uric acid elevation known with ACLY inhibition.

against.text: Myalgia lower with bempedoic acid (4.7% vs 7.2% placebo, f_503d2aa5493aa7). Overall AEs similar to placebo in phase 2 (f_c39167a04c4bfe). Absolute rates of tendon rupture and gout low; unclear if they would offset CV benefit.

hypotheses.would_settle: Full safety dataset at trial readout; incidence of tendon rupture, gout, and other serious AEs.

against.text: CLEAR Wisdom (statin-intolerant) baseline LDL-C 120.4 mg/dL (3.114 mmol/L, f_06c23b2a2c6517) matches Outcomes inclusion (LDL-C ≥100 mg/dL, f_1504a355043a6d). Statin-intolerant patients still derive CV benefit from LDL lowering (IMPROVE-IT, PCSK9 inhibitor subgroups).

hypotheses.would_settle: Subgroup analysis by baseline LDL-C and statin intolerance severity.

against.text: Standard MACE-4 endpoint, placebo-controlled, 3.5-year follow-up appropriate for LDL-lowering therapy (CTT shows benefit by 1-2 years). No crossover or active comparator. Trial not stopped early (f_26b1577ef81dfa).
Large sample (~14,000 randomized, f_66a8b978b68f8d, f_708f002aaa2c55), not stopped early (f_26b1577ef81dfa), no reported adherence or recruitment issues.
Robust phase 3 biomarker data in target population (CLEAR Wisdom, f_77a23c173de6bc), genetic validation (f_e5f10161df91fe), complete design parameters (events, follow-up, sample size).
Expected HR 0.896 with 60% power; upper CI likely near 1.0. Robust success requires upper CI well below 0.90.

for.text: Tendon rupture signal (0.5% vs 0%, f_f1b079c609ee14) and gout (f_36d2ad1fd3b9e1) could represent important safety caveats if confirmed at scale.

against.text: Absolute rates low; myalgia actually lower with drug (f_503d2aa5493aa7). Caveat status depends on final safety profile.

issues.issue: Baseline values for apoB (141.3 mg/dL), non-HDL-C (192.6 mg/dL), and hsCRP (2.9 mg/L) from CLEAR Serenity are not found in the abstract (Verifier: not_found), though they exist as verified facts from the full paper (pmcid:PMC6509724). Per protocol, missing phase 3 biomarker data in abstracts is a medium-severity caveat; inputs should be retained but flagged.
issues.request: Verify apoB, non-HDL-C, and hsCRP baseline values from CLEAR Serenity full text (pmcid:PMC6509724) and confirm they represent the statin-intolerant population at 180 mg dose.

issues.issue: Follow-up input of 3.5 years (42 months) comes from design paper (pmid:33470195) describing 'projected median treatment exposure of 42 months', not confirmed median follow-up. Actual follow-up in completed trial may differ.
issues.request: Add caveat that follow-up is projected treatment exposure from design paper; actual median follow-up will be known at readout.

issues.issue: Calculator inputs include apoB, non-HDL-C, and hsCRP changes with baselines, but calculator result shows basis='LDL-C' only. Secondary biomarker changes are not used in prediction and may confuse interpretation.
issues.request: Clarify whether secondary biomarker inputs are for context only or if a multi-biomarker pathway calculation was intended; consider removing unused inputs or documenting why they are included.
